en: The Theravāda Vinaya:
Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga,
Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Pregnant Women, 63.
The Training Rule for a Trainee Nun.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were ordaining a *sikkhamānā* who had not trained for two years in the six rules;
they were foolish and incompetent, and did not know what was allowable or what was unallowable.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as before]... complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
“How can nuns ordain a trainee nun who has not trained for two years in the six rules?
… [after questioning] … “Is it true, monks, that nuns ordain a trainee nun who has not trained for two years in the six rules?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“... How indeed, monks, can these bhikkhunīs give the full admission to a trainee nun who has not trained for two years in the six rules?
This, monks, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of those with faith... [and so on].
Having rebuked him … and having given a discourse on the Dhamma, he addressed the monks: “Monks,
I allow you to grant formal permission for a trainee nun (sikkhamānā) to train in the six rules for two years.”
And furthermore, monks, it should be given in this way:

That trainee nun (sikkhamānā), having approached the Saṅgha, having arranged her upper robe over one shoulder, having bowed at the feet of the bhikkhunīs, having sat down on her haunches and extended her hands in reverential salutation, should speak thus:
“Venerable ladies, I, so-and-so, am a trainee nun under Venerable so-and-so.”
‘I request the Saṅgha for permission to train in the six rules for two years.
It should be requested a second time;
it should be requested a third time.
The Saṅgha should be informed by a competent and experienced bhikkhunī:
“Let the noble Saṅgha hear me.
This trainee nun named so-and-so requests from the Saṅgha, through the noble lady named so-and-so, formal authorization to train in the six rules for two years.”
If it seems appropriate to the Saṅgha, let the Saṅgha grant permission for the training in the six rules for two years to the trainee nun named so-and-so.
This is the motion.
Let the noble Saṅgha hear me.
This trainee nun named so-and-so requests from the Saṅgha, through the venerable lady named so-and-so, formal authorization to train in the six rules for two years.
The Saṅgha grants formal authorization to the trainee nun named so-and-so to train in the six rules for two years.
Whichever venerable lady approves of granting formal authorization to the trainee nun named so-and-so to train in the six rules for two years, let her be silent.
"Whoever does not approve should speak.
The Saṅgha has granted the authorization for the trainee named so-and-so to train in the six rules for two years.
It is pleasing to the Saṅgha; therefore, by silence, I hold it thus."
That trainee nun (sikkhamānā) should be told: "Speak thus":
"For two years, without transgression, I undertake and observe the undertaking of abstaining from the destruction of life.
For two years, without transgression, I undertake and observe the undertaking of abstaining from taking what is not given."
For two years, having undertaken the undertaking without transgression, I undertake the abstention from unchastity.
For two years, having undertaken the undertaking without transgression, I undertake the abstention from false speech.
For two years, having undertaken the undertaking without transgression, I undertake the abstention from fermented and distilled liquors, which are the basis for negligence.
“I undertake the undertaking of the restraint from eating at improper times for two years, without transgression.
Then the Blessed One, having rebuked those bhikkhunīs in many ways for being difficult to support … [as before] … and so,
bhikkhus, the bhikkhunīs should recite this training rule thus:
“Whatever nun, however, should give the full admission to a *sikkhamānā* who has not trained for two years in the six rules, it is an offense entailing confession (*pācittiya*).
“Whatever nun” means whichever nun of such a kind... [and so forth].
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the kind of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Two years" means:
Two years.
"One who has not trained in the training" means either that the training was not given, or that the training, having been given, was corrupted.
“Should give the full admission” means:
she should confer the higher ordination.
If, thinking “I will give the full admission,” she seeks out a group, a preceptor, a bowl, or a robe, or if she demarcates a boundary, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
For the motion, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
For the two formal proclamations, there are offenses of wrong-doing.
At the conclusion of the formal proclamation, it is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) for the preceptor.
For the community and for the preceptor, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If she gives the full admission in a legitimate legal act while perceiving it as a legitimate legal act, there is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
If she gives the full admission in a legitimate legal act while being doubtful of it, there is an offense entailing expiation.

If it is a legitimate legal act (*dhammakamma*) and she perceives it as an illegitimate legal act (*adhammakamma*), yet she causes [the person] to leave [the saṅgha], there is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*).
If it is an illegitimate legal act and she perceives it as a legitimate legal act, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
If it is an illegitimate legal act and she is uncertain, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is an illegitimate legal procedure and one perceives it as such, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
There is no offense if one ordains a trainee nun (*sikkhamānā*) who has trained for two years in the six rules.
"In the case of one who is insane,
or in the case of a first-offender.
The third training rule is concluded.
